rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and 3AA label, but includes speculative image claims such as uneven TE, partial collapse, and lack of hatching/debris that may not be reliably inferable from a single static image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, male factor diagnosis, first cycle status, BMI, stress, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis; could be stronger on how sperm parameters and fresh-transfer context specifically modify expectations.

Reasoning is structured and mostly internally consistent, with prognosis tied to young age, morphology, and lining concerns; minor issues include some hedging and slight inconsistency around expansion-stage terminology.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: supports SET in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, avoids unsupported add-ons, and does not overcall PGT-A; minor deviations include somewhat confident implantation/live birth estimates from morphology alone.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support adherence, review of endometrial readiness, and sensible future workup if unsuccessful; useful though some suggestions remain general rather than protocol-specific.
